name: gg-02-sign-and-temperature-controls
title: Sign and temperature controls (Fig 7 & Fig 9)
question:
Are the two adversarial controls reproduced? (1) With NEGATIVE heterotypic tension (checkerboard,
Fig 7: gamma_ld=-3) the aggregate should intercalate and the heterotypic fraction should RISE —
the opposite of sorting. (2) At HIGH temperature (Fig 9: sorting energies at T=40) thermal
fluctuations should overwhelm the tension barriers and the aggregate should MIX rather than sort
cleanly. Do these behave as the paper predicts, and does the heterotypic-fraction order parameter
suffice to distinguish them from sorting?
hypothesis:
Checkerboard: heterotypic fraction rises (unlike cells prefer contact). High-T: sorting fails —
cells crumble/mix. If the heterotypic fraction alone cannot separate high-T mixing from sorting,
that is itself a finding about the order parameter's sufficiency.
investigation_role:
The falsification arms for gg-01. Sorting passes by direction + sign; these controls exist to try
to break that reading. Checkerboard flips the sign; high-T removes the clean sorting the metric
assumes. A control that behaves like sorting would collapse the interpretation.

run_config.runner: demo-style direct Composite execution (Node bridge); trajectories in runs/*.csv

readouts.name: heterotypic_fraction
readouts.description: Fraction of cell-cell boundary between unlike types.

readouts.name: mean_connectedness
readouts.description: Mean per-cell connected fraction; drops below 1.0 when cells crumble (mixing).

readouts.name: total_boundary
readouts.description: Total mismatched-bond boundary length; rises when the interface crumples.

behavior_tests.name: heterotypic-fraction-rises-under-checkerboard
behavior_tests.description: With negative heterotypic tension the fraction at 176 MCS exceeds its early value in every seed.

behavior_tests.name: high-temperature-degrades-cell-integrity
behavior_tests.description: At T=40 mean connectedness drops below the clean-sorting level (<0.98): the aggregate crumbles/mixes.

reproducibility_metrics.comparison:
3 seeds each, 176 MCS, 110 cells, 85x85 field. Initial = 8 MCS snapshot; final = 176 MCS.
Trajectories in runs/glazier_graner_{checkerboard,high_temperature}_seed{1,2,3}.csv.

metrics.note: Rises in all 3 seeds — the opposite sign to sorting. Clean sign control.

metrics.expected: mixing (sorted state dissolves), Glazier & Graner Fig 9 / Table II
metrics.note: hf FALLS by a magnitude comparable to sorting (-0.095 vs -0.100), so hf ALONE does not distinguish mixing from sorting at 176 MCS.
0.959 vs 0.998 for sorting — the discriminator. Total boundary also rises (4140 vs 3483).

findings.statement:
Sign control reproduced: with gamma_ld=-3 (checkerboard, Fig 7) the heterotypic fraction RISES
0.528 -> 0.671 (+27%, 3 seeds) — unlike cells intercalate, the opposite of sorting. This
confirms the direction of gg-01 is set by the sign of the heterotypic surface tension.

expected.summary: Negative heterotypic tension drives intercalation; heterotypic fraction increases (Fig 7).

findings.statement:
The high-temperature mixing regime (Fig 9) is only PARTIALLY separable on the heterotypic
fraction: at T=40 hf also falls (-20%, similar to sorting), so the order parameter alone cannot
tell thermal mixing from engulfment at 176 MCS. The distinguishing signal is in the secondary
observables — connectedness drops to 0.959 (vs 0.998 sorting) and total boundary rises to 4140
(vs 3483) — the boundary crumpling the paper describes.

evidence.observed: high-T: hf -0.095, connectedness 0.959, total_boundary 4140; sorting: hf -0.100, connectedness 0.998, total_boundary 3483
evidence.smoking_gun: connectedness 0.959 vs 0.998 separates mixing from sorting where hf does not

findings.explanation:
At T=40 fluctuations exceed the surface-tension barriers, so the interface reorganises by
crumbling rather than by clean engulfment; heterotypic contact still decreases, but cell
integrity is lost — which hf does not see and connectedness/bulk-moments do.
findings.next_action: Add a connectedness/bulk-moment mixing metric and run longer to separate the regimes quantitatively.

regression_compatibility.basis:
Both checkerboard and high_temperature composites build and run against the real Artistoo
engine for all 3 seeds; trajectories committed (runs/*.csv), chart renders.

biological_validation.basis:
Checkerboard sign-control PASSES cleanly (hf rises +27%, all seeds). High-T mixing is only
PARTIAL: reproduced in cell-integrity terms (connectedness 0.959, boundary rises) but NOT
separable from sorting on the heterotypic fraction alone (-0.095 vs -0.100). Honest partial,
not an inflated pass.

explanatory_gain.basis:
Establishes that the heterotypic fraction is a sufficient order parameter for the SIGN of
differential adhesion but NOT for the thermal-mixing transition, where a connectedness /
bulk-moment discriminator is required. Directly sharpens how the investigation's claims should
be read.

limitations: The high-T arm is under-resolved for a quantitative mixing claim: 176 MCS may be too short for the sorted vs mixed endpoints to diverge on hf, and no bulk-moment metric (paper Table II) is computed.
The high-T mixing claim rests on connectedness + total-boundary, not on the primary order parameter; the checkerboard sign control is clean.

literature_anchors.expectation: Negative heterotypic tension (checkerboard) drives intercalation; heterotypic fraction rises.
At high temperature the sorted state dissolves and the aggregate mixes (bulk moments blow up).
literature_anchors.status_in_workspace: Partial — connectedness drops to 0.959, but heterotypic fraction alone does not separate mixing from sorting

followup_proposals.title: Add a bulk-moment / connectedness mixing metric and run longer
followup_proposals.motivation:
The high-T arm shows the heterotypic fraction cannot distinguish thermal mixing from sorting at
176 MCS. A dedicated mixing discriminator (per Table II bulk moments) plus longer runs would
make the Fig-9 mixing transition a clean quantitative pass instead of a partial.
followup_proposals.hypothesized_mechanism:
Compute the aggregate's radial bulk moments (or a connectedness-weighted mixing index) each
snapshot; run >=1000 MCS; show sorting and high-T diverge on that metric even where hf coincides.
